decisions.location: Study 1, Materials (line 17); Study 1, Results and Discussion (lines 28, 30-35); References (lines 206-207)
decisions.quote: The present work focused on the GaN from Wynn's (1990Wynn's ( , 1992) ) studies with no intention to test the replicability of results coming from the other tasks (i.e., the Point-to-x task or the colour control task were not administered). However, two additional control tasks were administered to examine whether children could be limited by their knowledge of the verbal number sequence or their mastery of the cardinal word principle in counting (Wynn, 1990).
decisions.reason: Omitted replication target (resolving the prior schema validation error by supplying the canonical corrected_value fields with outcome set to cannot_be_determined). Rousselle and Vossius (2021) explicitly frame their work as a conceptual replication of the Give-a-Number (GaN) observations from both Wynn (1990) and Wynn (1992). Shipped row 365 represents only Wynn (1992) (10.1016/0010-0285(92)90008-p, Cognitive Psychology, which introduced the 7-month longitudinal design retested in Study 2). Wynn (1990) (10.1016/0010-0277(90)90003-3, Cognition) is a distinct primary empirical paper that introduced the GaN task and the cross-sectional counter vs. grabber strategy analysis. In Study 1 (Materials, lines 17-19; Results and Discussion, lines 28, 30-32, 34-35), the authors directly retest Wynn's (1990) counting vs. grabbing strategy predictions alongside the all-at-once cardinal generalization hypothesis attributed to Wynn (1990, 1992).

corrected_value.title: Effects of immediate-reinforcement training on delay discounting behavior in rats

decisions.quote:
A group of rats was exposed to an immediate (no-delay)-

reinforcement intervention and subsequent delay discounting

behavior was modestly, but statistically signiﬁcantly, more

impulsive compared to a control group. This is consistent

with previous work (Fox, 2022; Fox etal., 2019; Renda

etal., 2018; Smith etal., 2022), and with the conclusion
that prolonged exposure to immediate reinforcement may

have just modest impacts on subsequent impulsive choice,

compared to relatively larger impacts of exposure to delayed

reinforcement. This was true in the present experiment

despite double the number of subjects in each group and

double the number of immediate reinforcement training tri-

als, compared to previous research (Fox 2022; Fox etal.,

2019).
decisions.reason: Omitted replication target (no prior adjudication file existed). Fox (2024) is titled a systematic replication of immediate reinforcement training on delay discounting behavior in rats and uses the author's prior FR 2 immediate-reinforcement training vs. maturation/handling control and posttest signaled-RIFI delay-discounting paradigm. In the Introduction (lines 135-160) and Discussion (lines 524-549), the author explicitly identifies Fox (2022) (10.1002/jeab.727) and Fox et al. (2019) (10.1016/j.beproc.2018.11.009) as the previous research whose sample size per group and number of immediate-reinforcement training trials were doubled (with a 50% longer intervention duration) to test the limits and generality of their reported results, and compares the observed modest increase in impulsive choice directly against them. Shipped row 1480 covers only Renda et al. (2018) (10.1002/jeab.432), leaving Fox (2022) omitted.

decisions.location: Chapter 1, The Original Study (Gillies, 2018; Gillies & Dozois, 2021), Footnote 4 (lines 1406-1431)
decisions.quote:
The Gillies and Dozois (2021) citation references an article published following completion of the
master’s thesis, which is cited as Gillies (2018). Because the published article does not include the latent
growth modeling (LGM) analyses, both articles are referenced, with the Gillies (2018) citation referenced
when LGM analyses are specifically discussed.
decisions.reason: Alternate report of the same original study already represented by shipped row input_row_index 2628 (and blind target_index 0; no prior adjudication file existed). Shipped row 2628 codes Gillies (2018), 'Trajectories of the effects of sad mood induction procedures (MIPs) (Master’s Thesis)'. In Chapter 1, under the heading 'The Original Study (Gillies, 2018; Gillies & Dozois, 2021)' (line 1406), Footnote 4 (lines 1428-1431) explicitly explains that Gillies and Dozois (2021) (10.1016/j.jad.2021.05.047) is the journal article published following completion of the Gillies (2018) master's thesis reporting the same original N = 401 Western University study (minus the latent growth modeling analyses retained only in the thesis). Under the same-original / alternate-report rule, Gillies and Dozois (2021) does not represent a separate omitted original study.

decisions.quote: This study aimed to replicate research behind Climate Schools: Alcohol and Cannabis course among a large cohort of adolescents. METHODS: Seventy-one secondary schools across three States participated in a cluster-randomised controlled trial. Year 8 students received either the web-based Climate Schools: Alcohol and Cannabis course (Climate, n = 3236), or health education as usual (Control, n = 3150).
decisions.reason: The supplied source text (7252b65650fbd13d.txt) contains only the title, author list, abstract, and publisher reference list, with the note 'Publisher reference list (article body unavailable)' at line 6 (and no prior adjudication file existed). Although the abstract states that 'This study aimed to replicate research behind Climate Schools: Alcohol and Cannabis course among a large cohort of adolescents' and 'replicate alcohol effects in a large and diverse sample of students', it provides no in-text citations, while the reference list contains multiple distinct primary trials of the Climate Schools program by the same research group—including Newton et al. (2009) (10.1080/00048670802653364, Alcohol module, already present as shipped row 258), Newton et al. (2010) (10.1111/j.1360-0443.2009.02853.x, final results of the combined Alcohol and Cannabis course), Champion et al. (2015) (10.1177/0004867415577435, cross-validation trial of the internet-based alcohol and cannabis program), Teesson et al. (2017) (10.1017/S0033291717000198), and Newton et al. (2018) (10.1186/s13011-018-0171-4). Without the article body, the available evidence cannot establish which specific original work(s) were empirically retested as replication targets or whether any target beyond shipped row 258 was omitted.
